svg.title: How rules are evaluated
svg.desc: The rule evaluation loop for the six rule types (time schedule, idle unload, high load grow, low traffic shrink, make room by priority, auto heal). Every 10 seconds the jobs process that holds the rules lease ticks; each enabled rule is evaluated in priority order when its own interval is due; it reads its inputs (last request, requests per minute, queue and KV cache, free VRAM, health) and decides one outcome, recording why: no_match, cooldown, skipped, dry_run, fired or error. A fired rule hands its actions to the swap manager, which runs each as a safe swap. Every outcome goes to the history (rule runs, audit log, alerts), then the next tick starts. A dry run plans the same way without sending a command; cooldown is per rule and deployment, and at most two swaps run at once by default.
